newsitem.title: USA: U.S. disputes WTO challenge to Cuba law.
newsitem.headline: U.S. disputes WTO challenge to Cuba law.

text.p: The United States said on Wednesday that a WTO challenge to its Helms-Burton law against Cuba is a "lose-lose" proposition.
Earlier Wednesday in Geneva, the European Union and other U.S. allies succeeded in getting the World Trade Organization to establish a panel to study the validity of the Helms-Burton legislation.
"Many of us ... have made it clear that pursuing this course to the WTO is a lose-lose proposition," U.S. Commerce Undersecretary Stuart Eizenstat said at a business luncheon.
"This is essentially a political and policy dispute which needs to be resolved diplomatically, not by an institution designed to deal with trade disputes," Eizenstat added.
The United States enacted the Helms-Burton law in March shortly after the Cuban air force shot down two U.S. civilian aircraft over the Florida Straits.
The law, which tightened the U.S. embargo against Cuba, contains sanctions for foreign companies and investors that do business with disputed properties in Cuba.

The EU and countries such as Canada, Mexico and Australia hold that the U.S. legislation is extra-territorial, as it attempts to enforce U.S. penalties on companies and individuals acting outside its territory.

The U.S., however, argues that Helms-Burton sanctions are narrowly focused on firms and investors who obtain benefits from properties confiscated from U.S. citizens and corporations after the 1959 Cuban revolution.
Eizenstat said the dispute at the WTO would only incite protectionists in the United States.

Asked by reporters what the U.S. would do if the WTO ruled against it on the Helms-Burton dispute, he answered: "It's our belief that we won't have to face that case. We hope that we will be able to resolve it."
The United States could invoke a national interest waiver to avoid abiding by an adverse WTO ruling.
Eizenstat is scheduled to travel later Wednesday to Ireland to attend a followup meeting of a U.S.-EU conference, where the issue of Helms-Burton is likely to surface.
Eizenstat, as a special envoy appointed by President Clinton, is seeking U.S. allies' support to raise diplomatic pressure on Cuban President Fidel Castro.
The United States wants other countries to press Castro, the only communist leader in the Americas, to reform his one-party political system and to respect human rights.
